14 ICMBio SISBio records, no locality: 12 within 1 km of zoos in São Paulo, Sorocaba, Rio and Brusque (Wikidata Q3364798, Q1535754, Q10306230, Q121094903); 2 elsewhere. COL says Africa. Points to zoo animals, but the records don't name one.
Two NABU|naturgucker records, locality "Zoologischer Garten Frankfurt am Main": a zoo, so captive animals. They're every counted record here.

26 air-sampling DNA reads, 2023, from two Globe Institute airDNA experiments, no locality, none within 10 km of a zoo on Wikidata for the points checked. They document no animal; COL says Africa. Misidentified or contaminant reads are likely, not stated.
Two KTH 18S reads from Baltic Sea metabarcoding, 2016 and 2017: DNA from water, so no chimpanzee was there; misidentified or contaminant reads, as in 56:NU. They're every counted record here.

Of 85 records, 79 are marked captive and 71 are in New Mexico; all 20 we read name a zoo (Albuquerque, "Captive at San Francisco Zoo"). The 5 other unmarked ones, from other museums, are unread, so this can't be high. COL says Africa.

Five records: three name a zoo (Point Defiance, San Antonio, Hogle). An INSDC genome sits 0.5 km from Bronx Zoo (Wikidata Q739792), and an iBOL GenBank sequence has no locality. Wikidata has this species in Africa. Those two are inferred, not stated.

11 air-sampling DNA reads, 2024–25, CSIRO, Canberra: 3 are 0.09 km from the National Zoo & Aquarium (Wikidata Q495039), 8 at another point with no zoo within 1 km. They document no free animal; COL doesn't list Oceania. Inferred from dataset and coordinates.

Two records: a Bavarian State Collection sample from Tierpark Hellabrunn, 2011, and NABU|naturgucker "Tempelhof Nord", a Berlin district, 2024, with no wild or captive mark. COL says Africa; Southern Asia. The second is inferred, not stated.

32 records: 30 in the Global Roadkill dataset, the 20 we read with field localities in Iran to 2023, plus an iNaturalist record from Semnan with a field remark and an FMNH specimen. Three datasets, no captive sign, and COL lists Southern Asia. The flag comes from the core being Africa.

Three Natuurmuseum Brabant specimens: "Hilvarenbeek" twice (5 km uncertainty, 7.8 km from Safaripark Beekse Bergen, Wikidata Q2183630) and "'s-Hertogenbosch", 1992. Town localities with no wild sign, as in 25:NL; points to kept animals, but the records don't say so.

Of 56 records, 46 are marked captive and 44 are MSB specimens in New Mexico; all 20 we read say Albuquerque BioPark Zoo. Nine unmarked ones, including other museums' specimens, are unread, so this can't be high. COL says Africa; Southern Asia.

Two NABU|naturgucker records: "Zoologischer Garten Berlin", 2007, and a grid-cell locality at 54.18, 7.90 (Helgoland), 2024, no captive mark. Wikidata has this species endemic to China. The second looks like a misidentification or data error, but the record doesn't say so.

Four NABU|naturgucker map-sheet or town records, 2008–2016, no captive or wild mark: two 2.1 km from Zoo Halle (Wikidata Q220245), two (Langebrück, Illertissen) with no zoo within 3 km. COL says Africa. Too thin to call, so it stays.

Two records: an NHMD tusk whose remarks say it was confiscated in a Copenhagen court case, 1988, and one air-sampling DNA read, 2022. The first is stated by the record; the read documents no animal, but doesn't say so. COL says Africa.

Four sequence records (two iBOL, two INSDC), 2007, at one point in Warsaw, no locality. Remarks give vouchers "PL-IGAB-ZBM" and subspecies "knochenhaueri", so likely a Polish lab's material, not an animal seen in Poland. COL says Africa. Inferred, not stated.

Seven records: Columbus, Brookfield and San Antonio zoos by name; an INSDC genome 0.2 km from Louisville Zoo (Wikidata Q3576024); Seattle's "Watoto", "animal still alive", a named individual. Seattle (2014) and Ogden (1905) give only a city. COL says Africa. Inferred for those.

Four ICMBio SISBio records, 2017–2019, São Paulo, no locality, all at one point 0.3 km from São Paulo Zoo (Wikidata Q3364798). COL says Africa. Points to zoo animals, but the records themselves don't name one.
Of 95 records, 94 are marked captive; 89 are MSB specimens in New Mexico, and all 20 we read say Albuquerque BioPark Zoo. One unmarked record, unread, keeps this from high. COL says Africa.

Two undated MNHN (Paris) specimens with no locality, at one point 0.1 km from Paris Zoological Park (Wikidata Q1969385). COL says Africa. Points to zoo animals, but the records themselves don't name one.

245 records: 179 Borror Lab sound recordings, all 20 we read in zoo pens and yards (Columbus, Pittsburgh, Potter Park, Brookfield); 64 iBOL sequences and 2 specimens unread. No captive field filled, and COL says Africa. The rest is inferred, not stated.

All 390 are EEZA (CSIC, Almería) specimens in one ungulate collection, 1971–2008; all 20 we read say "Almería; Finca La Hoya", one farm address. COL says Africa. Points to a herd kept at the institute, but no record says captive, and 370 are unread.
Seven specimens, and each names a zoo: Oakland (2), Honolulu (2), Hogle, San Antonio, Houston. The records themselves name the zoos, and they're every counted record here.

An Ibaraki Nature Museum specimen, Kumamoto, 1998, no locality, and an iBOL record "Mined from GenBank", coordinates near the middle of Japan. Neither documents a free animal, and COL says South America. Inferred from the record types, not stated.

Two NABU|naturgucker records: "Luisenpark - Mannheim", 2018, a park that keeps animals, and a former military site in Berlin, 2015, a field locality with no captive mark: likely a released animal. One dataset, and COL says Middle America, so no second source agrees.

Two Auckland Museum specimens, 1980, no locality, coordinates with 800 km uncertainty, so they name only the country. A kept animal can't be told from a free one here, and COL says Middle America. Too thin to call, so it stays.
